scope: Focused review of November 18–19 outcomes and reactions. It covered House leadership and oversight, Republican succession, chip licensing, Gulf tensions, the Shenzhen talks, temporary protection for Venezuelans and military cooperation with Caracas. Several court and implementation outcomes remain open.
summary: House Democrats nominated Jeffries for speaker. Commerce put a new licensing requirement into effect for advanced chips, and Trump met Xi and Putin in Shenzhen. Hegseth announced military cooperation with Caracas. The administration applied for Supreme Court relief in the Venezuelan temporary protection dispute. Vance’s outreach to El-Sayed and Trump’s praise of Rubio matter for the Republican succession discussion. The original report on Trump’s private reaction was inaccessible. Venezuela’s election timetable, several operative court outcomes and actual enforcement remain open. Later orders in the Cook and Project Rousseau cases, Big Bend construction and Massie’s next House action remain unverified.
editorial_notes: Reviewed distinct actor-led titles and clarified what remains pending in election, military, court and personnel passages.

Replaced obsolete chip-rule publication language, named the House leadership jobs, explained temporary protection and clarified the difference between testimony, preservation and votes to remove an official.
